verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance publishes a public, keyless OpenAPI v3 document, confirmed by probe as a full 681K-character spec that includes registered-agent-deliveries endpoints. It also documents OAuth client-credentials auth for server-to-server use, rate-limit headers, and idempotency keys, which is solid support for programmatic driving. However, create, update and delete operations need capabilities that Harbor must explicitly grant, so full write control is not self-serve. missing for 10: self-serve write access without vendor grant, independent hands-on corroboration of successful API calls.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: a public, keyless OpenAPI document for the Harbor Compliance API (OAuth-authenticated at runtime)
For server-to-server integrations. Exchange your client ID and secret at /api/v3/oauth/access_token with grant_type=client_credentials
Endpoints marked as idempotent accept an optional Idempotency-Key header, so a request can be retried safely
Honor Retry-After before retrying. Monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining and throttle before hitting zero
